dossier.claim: Several English choices blur Kojirou’s distinctive swordsmanship and legendary identity. The clearest changes replace his exceptional stance, attack paths, and reach advantage with different descriptions. These do not establish a general loss of either skill or cultivated bearing.
dossier.sourcePattern: The Japanese distinguishes technique from equipment or raw power: Assassin freely handles a long weapon, follows curved attack paths, controls a greater fighting range, and adopts one exceptional stance despite ordinarily having none. His own description calls that technique unorthodox. The account of his legendary identity also places him as a celebrated master’s rival.
dossier.englishEffect: The English turns the unique stance into an imaginary one, trajectories into blade shapes, and a range differential into physical separation. Reels obscures dexterous handling, while wicked leaves his departure from orthodox technique unspecified. His legendary rival role becomes a world-ranking claim.
dossier.limits: These examples do not show that the English consistently diminishes Assassin’s skill or erases his cultivated manner. Nearby sentences recover the trajectory comparison, and his control of Saber’s approach remains evident. The deliberate strike against her sword and his refusal to stain her with blood preserve tactical agency and personal courtesy. His farewell and warning about outside interference admit defensible literary recastings and are excluded. The skull-masked Assassin’s wishes and battles, and the prologue’s spear mechanics, concern different subjects and supply no evidence for this Kojirou claim.
dossier.diagnostic: 30 findings in this category; 6 cited passages.
